context: a letter from Frederick Behrens, which you are answering
exchanges:
I presume you are much plagued by applications for your autograph, and if, by adding one more to the list of your troublesome admirers, you deem it too great a liberty, pray excuse me—but grant my request.

I have long been a great admirer of your genius and ever since I have been a collector of autographs, it has been my ardent wish to have yours.

By conferring upon me this favour, you will greatly oblige,

Yours very faithfully | Frederick Behrens—

Charles Darwin, Esqre | F.R.S. Etc.
Mr. Darwin has much pleasure in sending the subjoined signature. | Charles Darwin
